2.  As per the office report dated 16.5.2023, notice sent to the informant has been served personally.
3. In the interest of justice, learned counsel for the applicant is permitted to correct the memorandum of the anticipatory bail application, during the course of the day.

4. Heard Ms. Nidhi Rai, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri V.K.S. Parmar, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as perused the record.

1 5. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No. 270 of 2020, registered under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and 3/4(2) POCSO Act at Police Station- Mubarakpur, District- Azamgarh with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

6. As per prosecution story, the report was lodged by the informant regarding disappearance of his minor daughter on 1.12.2020 at about 09:00 p.m.
7.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that he has been falsely implicated in this case.
The FIR is delayed by about three days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
The applicant and the victim had married before the Registrar of Marriage, Ghaziabad and the victim was major at the time of incident as her date of birth is 14.1.2002.
Learned counsel has further stated that even the ossification test report indicates her age to be above 18 years.
The statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. categorically indicates that she had gone with the applicant out of her own sweet-will.
The instant case is misuse of process of the Court.
8. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
The applicant has apprehension of his arrest.

Learned counsel has stated that the applicant undertakes that he has co-operated in the investigation and is ready to do so in trial also failing which the State can move appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail.
9. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application but unable to dispute the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant.

10. On due consideration to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and considering the nature of accusations and antecedents of the applicant, the applicant is liable to be enlarged on anticipatory bail in view of the judgment of Supreme Court in the case of "Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1".

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The future contingencies regarding the anticipatory bail being granted to applicant shall also be taken care of as per the aforesaid judgment of the Apex Court.
11. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
